title: Zone controller failure before a resort opening
problem: A zone controller failed overnight and left the east wing of a 180-room resort without cooling two months before its scheduled opening. Rooms could not be handed over until every zone held its set temperature.
fix: We isolated the fault to the controller, replaced it with a matching unit, and checked refrigerant pressures and airflow across all 46 indoor units in the wing. Each zone was tested against its design range before we released the system.
result: The east wing opened on schedule. All 46 indoor units run inside their design range, and the owner received a written commissioning report.

title: Preventive maintenance contract for a six-floor office
problem: Tenant complaints about uneven temperatures rose every summer. Repeated call-outs cost more than a planned service plan would have.
fix: We set up a quarterly preventive maintenance schedule covering filters, coils, and pressure checks on every VRF outdoor and indoor unit. Each visit produced a logged report with readings against manufacturer limits.
result: Emergency call-outs dropped to zero over the first 12 months, and the building manager now plans the service budget a year ahead.
metricLabel: Emergency call-outs in the first 12 months

title: Phased retrofit of an aging apartment block
problem: An apartment block of 60 units had aging split systems and a failing central plant. Running costs were rising and residents were losing comfort on hot days.
fix: We replaced the plant in three phases, floor by floor, so residents kept cooling during the work. Controls were upgraded to schedule each zone by occupancy.
result: Energy use fell by about 30 percent in the first year, and no unit was without cooling for more than one day.
metricLabel: Reduction in energy use in year one
